title: Arrays & List Data Structures
description: Arrays and lists store ordered elements in contiguous memory blocks with O(1) random index access.

codeExamples.python:
numbers = [10, 20, 30, 40, 50]
numbers.append(60)
first_item = numbers[0]
sub_slice = numbers[1:4]
print(f'First: {first_item}, Slice: {sub_slice}, Full List: {numbers}')

quiz.question: What is the time complexity of accessing an element by index in a contiguous array?
options: O(1) constant time because element memory address is directly computed using base_address + index * element_size.
O(N) linear time scanning from index 0.
quiz.explanation: Arrays provide O(1) random access by computing pointer offsets directly from index multiplication.

interviewQuestions.q: 01. What is the difference between a Dynamic Array (Python list / C++ vector) vs Fixed-Size Array?
interviewQuestions.a: Fixed-size arrays allocate a permanent memory block at creation. Dynamic arrays allocate an initial capacity; when full, they automatically allocate a double-sized memory block and copy existing elements over (Amortized O(1) append time).

interviewQuestions.q: 02. How is a Python list implemented internally in CPython?
interviewQuestions.a: CPython lists are variable-length array of 64-bit memory pointers (PyObject*) stored in a contiguous C array block on the Heap, not contiguous raw primitive values.

interviewQuestions.q: 03. What is the time complexity of array operations (Access, Search, Insert at Start, Insert at End)?
interviewQuestions.a: Access: O(1). Search: O(N). Insert at End (Append): Amortized O(1). Insert at Start (Prepend): O(N) because all N existing elements must shift right in memory.

interviewQuestions.q: 04. What is the difference between Shallow Copy vs Deep Copy of a list in Python?
interviewQuestions.a: Shallow copy (`copy.copy(lst)` or `lst[:]`) creates a new list container pointing to the SAME nested objects in memory. Deep copy (`copy.deepcopy(lst)`) recursively duplicates all nested objects.

interviewQuestions.q: 05. Why is deleting an element from the middle of an array an O(N) operation?
interviewQuestions.a: Deleting an element leaves an empty slot; all subsequent elements past the deleted index must shift left by 1 position in memory to maintain contiguous layout.

interviewQuestions.q: 06. How does Python Slicing (`list[start:stop:step]`) work under the hood?
interviewQuestions.a: Slicing constructs a new list object containing references to the selected element range. `step = -1` reverses the array (`list[::-1]`).

interviewQuestions.q: 07. What is CPU Cache L1/L2 Locality of Reference (Spatial Locality) in contiguous arrays?
interviewQuestions.a: Because array elements sit adjacent in RAM, loading one element fetches an entire 64-byte Cache Line into CPU L1 cache, making sequential array processing significantly faster than linked lists.

interviewQuestions.q: 08. What is the difference between `append()` vs `extend()` in Python lists?
interviewQuestions.a: `append(x)` adds `x` as a SINGLE element at the end of the list. `extend(iterable)` iterates through `iterable` and appends EACH element individually.

interviewQuestions.q: 09. How does Two Pointer Technique optimize array search problems from O(N²) to O(N)?
interviewQuestions.a: By initializing left (0) and right (N-1) pointers moving inward on sorted arrays, two pointers eliminate unnecessary nested loop iterations (e.g. Container With Most Water, Two Sum).

interviewQuestions.q: 10. What is Sliding Window Technique on arrays?
interviewQuestions.a: Sliding Window maintains a running window (sub-segment) across an array to solve sub-array sum or maximum problems in O(N) linear time instead of recalculating overlapping sub-arrays.

interviewQuestions.q: 11. What is the difference between `list.sort()` vs `sorted()` in Python?
interviewQuestions.a: `list.sort()` sorts the list in-place (mutating original list) returning `None`. `sorted(list)` returns a BRAND NEW sorted list leaving the original list unchanged.

interviewQuestions.q: 12. What sorting algorithm is used by Python's `sort()` method?
interviewQuestions.a: Python uses **Timsort**, a hybrid adaptive algorithm derived from Merge Sort and Insertion Sort with O(N log N) worst-case and O(N) best-case performance.

interviewQuestions.q: 13. What is a Matrix (2D Array) and how is Row-Major vs Column-Major ordering stored in memory?
interviewQuestions.a: 2D arrays are stored in 1D contiguous RAM. Row-Major (C/Python) stores elements row-by-row (`index = row * cols + col`). Column-Major (Fortran/MATLAB) stores column-by-column.

interviewQuestions.q: 14. What is Array Resizing Factor and Over-allocation in dynamic arrays?
interviewQuestions.a: To avoid resizing on every `append()`, dynamic arrays allocate extra spare capacity using growth factors (CPython uses growth factor ~1.125 + 6, C++ std::vector uses 2.0 or 1.5).

interviewQuestions.q: 15. What is the difference between Python `array` module vs standard `list`?
interviewQuestions.a: The `array` module stores compact homogeneous primitive C-types directly in memory without pointer wrapping, consuming 4-8x less RAM memory.

interviewQuestions.q: 16. What is NumPy ndarray and why is it preferred for data science?
interviewQuestions.a: NumPy arrays store fixed-type contiguous binary data blocks executed via SIMD C/Fortran vector operations, running up to 100x faster than standard Python list loops.

interviewQuestions.q: 17. How does Binary Search on a sorted array achieve O(log N) complexity?
interviewQuestions.a: By halving the search space at every step (`mid = (low + high) // 2`), binary search finds targets in O(log N) time instead of linear O(N) scanning.

interviewQuestions.q: 18. What is In-Place Array Reversal algorithm?
interviewQuestions.a: Swap elements from opposite ends (`arr[left]`, `arr[right]`) moving inward until `left >= right`, modifying array in O(1) auxiliary space.

interviewQuestions.q: 19. How to find Duplicate Elements in an array in O(N) time and O(1) extra space?
interviewQuestions.a: Floyd's Tortoise and Hare Cycle Detection algorithm treats array values as pointer indices to locate duplicate entry cycles.

interviewQuestions.q: 20. What are production best practices when working with Lists and Arrays?
interviewQuestions.a: Pre-allocate array capacity when size is known, avoid `insert(0, val)` on large lists (use `collections.deque` for O(1) prepends), and leverage vectorized NumPy operations for mathematical processing.
